response:
1. PREMISE: Your framing treats the letter as the core decision when the actual decision is whether to declare a comprehensive demand for commitment before establishing whether she has moved on from you. The hidden assumption is that your internal recognition of what you want now constitutes information she needs immediately to make decisions about her own future. The entire analysis turns on whether your revelation serves her capacity to choose freely or pressures her choice by front-loading your five years of regret into a moment when she has just begun cautiously reconnecting with you.

2. STAKES: Julie stands to lose her ability to explore renewed contact with you without the weight of your accumulated longing shaping every interaction—she may feel obligated to manage your emotional recovery rather than assess what she actually wants. You stand to face either acceptance that resolves your five-year regret or rejection that confirms your fear of irretrievable loss, eliminating the ambiguity you currently inhabit. Your sister stands to host a gathering now freighted with relationship crisis regardless of her preferences. Any future child of yours with Julie would be born into a relationship formed under pressure rather than mutual discovery. Your coworkers and Julie's social circle will receive the narrative of your public emotional declaration and its outcome.

3. DIRECTIVE: Do not deliver the letter at the party. The constraint on your action is that she has signaled reluctance to accelerate involvement, and deploying a written declaration of five-year-old feelings after one month of resumed contact will convert her hesitation into a response obligation rather than a genuine opening.
[Rejected path: deliver the letter at the party expressing love and commitment demands. This produces immediate pressure on her to either reciprocate your declared emotional trajectory or reject you publicly in your social space and hers; probability of primary harm: high.]

4. RECOMMENDATION: Spend the next two months in ordinary contact with Julie without written declarations, allowing her to initiate acceleration of the relationship or to maintain distance. The letter forces her to process not what she wants but what you need her to want, whereas sustained ordinary interaction—conversations, shared time, genuine listening to whether her life direction has changed—permits her to separate her authentic interest in you from her empathy for your regret. You describe her as your best friend; a best friend deserves the chance to want you back for reasons that originate in her own recognition, not in your delivery of a five-year emotional ledger. The cost is sustained uncertainty and the genuine possibility that she may choose not to pursue this. The competing claim—that clarity about your intentions demonstrates integrity and respects her time—fails because intentionality expressed prematurely is indistinguishable from pressure. Therefore: attend the party as a person who is simply glad to reconnect with someone important, not as a person conducting a transaction in which you announce your terms and await her verdict.
